title: GPU edge tiling & allocation playbook — sprint journal
summary: Weekly sprint journal capturing the 'edge tiling' allocation experiment, capacity implications across EU/US/APAC, recent preemption event, and next-step playbook items for smoothing latency for small inference jobs.
content:
Purpose: capture week-of sprint notes for edge-tiling pilot (pack small inference tasks into fractional GPU tiles), record run metrics, decisions, and owners. High-level goal: reduce tail latency for small requests and improve packing efficiency without increasing preemption risk for reserved workloads.

Attendees: Aisha P (owner), Miguel O, Lena F, Devon S, Priya M, on-call: rachel.s, capacity: jared.b (async)

1) Experiment status — edge-tiling v1 (fractions via MIG-like soft-tiling)
- Run window: 2026-09-28 -> ongoing; traffic split: 5% prod-like, 10% synthetic microburst.
- Observations: median latency for <128-token requests down ~12% in EU region; 95th percentile improved in US-west but worsened slightly in APAC under heavy burst.
- Efficiency: token-per-GPU-second improved ~18% for small batch workloads in test buckets.
- Cost signal: provisional per-token cost reduced for small-models; need precise binning before extrapolation.

Known risk: when APAC region had an unexpected preemption window (see incident below), the tile consolidation step triggered higher eviction churn — we think policy threshold is too aggressive at 40% reclaim.

2) Incident: APAC preemption spike — 2026-10-02 03:12 UTC
- Impact: ~4300 requests requeued over 12m; affected low-priority tiled pods. No SLA breach for Dedicated customers (isolated by priority bands).
- Root cause hypothesis: cloud preemption pattern coincided with tile rebalancer run (cron) + conservative reclaim threshold.
- Immediate mitigation taken: raised reclaim threshold from 40%->55% for tiled pool, disabled global rebalancer for 30m, pushed hotfix to controller to add jitter.
- Action items: fine-tune reclaim thresholds per region (owner: Miguel O, due: 2026-10-08), add synthetic preemption test in staging (owner: Lena F, due: 2026-10-11).

3) Capacity notes and regional outlook
- EU: demand steady, spare margin ~12% for the week; prewarming metric healthy. Consider shifting 2 spare tiles from US-east to EU in next allocation cycle if forecasts hold. (owner: jared.b, action: allocation request to procurement, due: 2026-10-09)
- US-east/west: predictable daytime burst; western edge shows higher variance. We'll pilot adaptive burst slots for US-west for 2 weeks. (owner: Devon S)
- APAC: tight margins during APAC primetime; current tiling improvement helps small-job efficiency but increases churn risk. Plan to run a scaled dry-run of reduced rebalancer frequency for 48h starting 2026-10-07. (owner: Priya M)

4) Playbook updates (draft edits captured here)
- New steps for tiled-pool incident response:
  - Stage 1: detect preemption-correlated rebalancer activity (automated rule)
  - Stage 2: auto-suspend rebalancer and queue manual review if >5% eviction rate in 10m
  - Stage 3: fallback routing: route small jobs to best-effort single-tenant micro-instances when tiled-pool below target fill
- Note: these are draft, still need SRE sign-off and runbook numbering. (SRE reviewer: rachel.s)

5) Scheduling and rollout plan for next week
- 2026-10-07: start 48h reduced-rebalancer frequency in APAC (Priya)
- 2026-10-08: threshold tuning and canary deploy of reclaim policy (Miguel)
- 2026-10-09: procurement allocation request for EU spare tiles (Jared)
- 2026-10-11: add preemption synthetic test to staging & run 3 cycles (Lena)
- 2026-10-12: checkpoint meeting + metrics readout (Aisha)

6) Metrics to capture for next checkpoint
- median and p95 latency for <128-token requests by region
- eviction/restart rate for tiled pods per hour
- token-per-GPU-second and cost-per-request delta vs baseline
- prewarming hit rate and coldstart tail events during bursts

7) Open questions / discussion points
- How to reconcile tile consolidation frequency vs. regional preemption patterns? Proposal: make consolidation frequency region-aware and governed by a preemption heatmap. (ask: research team for feasibility)
- Should dedicated customers be given opt-out from tiled pools even if on shared racks? (SA engagement required — Priya to start outreach)

8) Quick standup snippets from engineers
- Miguel: "Threshold tuning looks good in local sim, need safe canary for controller bump."
- Lena: "Synthetic preemption harness needs more realistic timing shapes — capturing actual cloud provider spikes."
- Devon: "US-west burst slots prototype ready; will push for limited canary behind feature flag."
- Priya: "Working on stakeholder comms for Dedicated opt-out; drafting proposal."

9) Action items (short list)
- MIG-style tile reclaim thresholds per region — Miguel O — due 2026-10-08
- APAC reduced rebalancer dry-run 48h — Priya M — start 2026-10-07
- Procurement ask to shift 2 tiles to EU — jared.b — request by 2026-10-09
- Staging preemption synthetic test — Lena F — due 2026-10-11
- Draft playbook page with explicit runbook steps and SRE sign-off — Aisha P + rachel.s — checkpoint 2026-10-12

Appendix: quick raw numbers from canary (09/29 - 10/03)
- EU small-job median latency: baseline 82ms -> tiled 72ms
- US-west p95 small-job latency: baseline 320ms -> tiled 280ms
- APAC p95 small-job latency: baseline 290ms -> tiled 305ms (note degradation under burst)
- Eviction spike during preemption window: tiled-pool eviction rate 4.6% (baseline pool 0.8%)

Notes-to-self: keep experiment traffic split conservative until we validate reclaim policy; ensure Dedicated customers' routes have guaranteed fallback to non-tiled pool.

Links and references: Jira INFRA-3221 (edge-tiling experiment), RFC on tiling design in Confluence, PR #1287 runtime tweaks, slack thread #infra-edge-tiling

End of journal entry.
decisions: 1) Disable global rebalancer temporarily during high preemption risk windows. 2) Increase reclaim threshold for tiled pool from 40% to 55% as a short-term mitigation. 3) Run region-aware rebalancer frequency experiment in APAC first.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: tile consolidation during provider preemption increases eviction churn. Mitigations: region-aware consolidation frequency, synthetic preemption tests, auto-suspend rebalancer when eviction rate spikes.
